questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
It was important to me that the city was a central capital of Europe. 

And that the University of my choice had a good reputation internationally.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The University did not at all live up to a required minimum standard of education within the EU. 

The facilities were old and worn out. The administration process was a complete disaster for all international students. 

The local students were not very welcoming. 

The teachers were unhelpful and had no compassion nor understanding for international students. 

ERASMUS students were generally seen more as a burden than an asset.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
It was insanely difficult. 

I was contacting the administration of the host University several times upon arrival, but they were not able to give me the necessary information. I was told that I was welcome to cancel my exchange one week before my arrival, because they were annoyed with my amount of questions. 

It should be mentioned, that my questions were just normal concerns of an ERASMUS student. I was only informed about the schedule for the welcome week one day before it took place. It learned that it is very typical French, but the administration is clearly not suited to welcome this amount of exchange students.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Depending on your budget I would use AirBnb, Seloger etc.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you don't know people in the city beforehand I would recommend to live in Cité Universitaire. Here it is much easier to get to know other students etc. If on the other hand you are more interested in the "local-experience" i would recommend to rent an apartment within the arrondissements 1-9, and just live the local life there.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not use it, but I heard great things from other ERASMUS students about cité universitaire. Do be aware that the rooms are very small, and might not be very sanitary.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was fairly easy to change courses once you had arrived. Just get it approved by your home university and then ask for a change at the local afterwards, since they are not keen to change anything without approval of the home university.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
The register you depending on the courses in your learning agreement. The enrollment is therefore fairly easy, and they also register you automatically to the exams. 

If you however wish to change your courses, you should change your learning agreement, getting it approved by your home university before it can be approved by the host university.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could contact the administration physically and online via e-mail. It should though be mentioned that they are not very responsive and you might need to push through several times in order to get an answer. Also patience will take you a long way, since the French in general is not good at planning too much ahead and therefore will only take care of urgent things.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
I would not at all recommend this host institution. I had lived in France before and knew people and the French mentality. But for a lot of other exchange students the stay was a complete nightmare. 

The law campus is far away in a sketchy neighborhood, the school facilities are old and worn out - and even the local students called it a prison. There is no understanding of the fact that you are a foreign student. It is not possible to retake exams if you fail. The French school system is very different, a lot of exams are without notes. Also the amount of ECTS for courses is very low, so you might need to take between 10-12 different courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I signed up for a LL.M program with evening courses and exams on saturdays, without knowing before I arrived. There was a total of 10 exams. Not what I would recommend for an exchange student who also wants to experience the city and meet new people

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses were very similar to the danish. The main difference was the amount of exams, the fact that you don't use books but only have the notes you take during classes. And these notes are only for revision before an exam since most exams did not allow use of notes.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very old school. Long lectures without participation. A few courses had presentations from the students. In general did the teachers not have much respect for the students

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer: I did not participate - would recommend to search for this outside of the host institution. Everything administrative is a complete chaos even signing of for non-academic stuff.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: none.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Would recommend to take long walks and get to know the city. 
Visit museums. 
Read a book in a parc or café. 
Enjoy an apero and make friends with strangers in cafés and restaurants.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The locals are very different. They can come of as cold, but they are just not very good at small talk. If you like good conversations about interesting topics that chances are that you get to know them, and after that they are so welcoming and invites you with them all around.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The students are very particular and very competitive.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The fact that they do not plan ahead and only take care of urgent things.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That they are very present and good at not taking small things as big problems.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: I would not at all recommend this university. Administrative chaos - even the local students are complaining. Go to Assas instead, also has a better academic reputation.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't apply for an exchange here.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: That I learned things about the French academic culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being an Erasmus student in this University.

Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
